roadmap.goal: A developer runs only the fast tier while editing and gets an answer in seconds on both stacks. Every test that boots a host, needs a container or calls a real system carries the one Integration category through a shared base class, a misplaced backend test fails the build, and CI runs exactly what it runs today.
roadmap.notes: Rigor profile thorough: pass model explicitly on every dispatch, the profile's agent_model for crafters and reviewer_model for reviewers. Every step is executed by a crafter, so finalize finds phase entries for each; no step is orchestrator-only. A push is not a step: the orchestrator makes it after the step named in that step's implementation_notes, and the next step opens by checking the delta records that push as judged. No non-test code changes in any slice (guarantee 1 of the delta, an allow-list). Mutation per slice: A N/A (package.json and docs); B N/A (a test helper, tests, workflow, shell, docs); C N/A (test files only); D N/A (test files only); E N/A (test files only); F N/A for Stryker, which mutates the product assembly (Test-Fast.ps1 is shell; the Python scripts carry their own unit tests). The list run: before every push from push 2 on, the step before the push runs the always-on clause A locally once, keeps its TRX as that push's id list and compares it locally with the list before; a difference stops the push. It is also the whole-suite gate. 8 such runs in the Story (L0 with the old clause, L2 to L7 with A, H once), about 350 s and 3.6 GB each, one at a time, never beside any other test run, frontend or backend, no token variable set. No other step runs an unfiltered or standard-filter dotnet test. CI's CSV is a cross-check, compared CI with CI, never with a local list. Every restricted run states a nonzero count read from the TRX, because dotnet test exits 0 on no match. Diffs: Passed ids must match, so a test that starts skipping counts as lost; a foreign commit excuses a line only if its diff shows that exact test removed; a test this Story added is named in the delta; unstable names compare per-class counts. Push plan: push 1 after 01-01, no backend run; push 2 after 03-01, slice B with the 14 live classes, THE ONE LIVE-SUITE PUSH, force-full with every connector; push 3 after 03-02, the scan move alone, the first plain run, judged against T0 for live and regular tests only; push 4 after 03-03, the hosted commit, which waits for one green plain run with no difference from T0; push 5 after 04-05; push 6 after 05-04; push 7 after 06-05. Pushes 3 to 7 are plain, and before each the push's diff goes through path-classifier.sh with every connector answer false. Push 3 waits for foreign runs started since push 2 to end green; if it still runs force-full it is judged as the live push, and the way out is 04-01's commit pulled forward or a foreign backend-path push, never the hosted commit. No other push on trunk while push 2 runs, and no live run or Linear key use for an hour before it (T12's last push edits ci_frontend.yml and is a live run too). A foreign force-full run is written down and does not break the one-live-push count; a force-full run of this Story's own making does. This Story leaves Lighthouse.Backend.Tests.csproj untouched; an NUnit or adapter change on trunk re-runs the probe's Live fixture before the next push. On a red push 2: grep TooManyRequests, wait the hour, re-run the failed job, never push. Two steps wait for the maintainer and no answer means they wait: 02-02 on the fast filter, 05-03 on the containers. A conflict with trunk stops the step and reports; nothing is rebased. No nWave scenario tag in any test title, comment or file. The filter strings, guarantees, probe table, stop rules and closing list are in feature-delta.md, sections Wave: DISTILL, and its section Review revision overrides the rest. Step 03-02 carries the scan move that DESIGN placed in slice D (D-6512-23).

The old script (git show of the commit before 06-02) and the new one over 05-04's TRX files give fully_qualified_name columns that cmp finds byte-identical
The new trx_to_csv.py over 05-04's TRX files reads every hosted row Integration and every fast and offline row Unit, both directions
Backend medians per category are re-cut from a CSV and written in the delta
Test-Fast.ps1 -NoBuild: median of 5 warm runs on a quiet machine at the default worker cap, with test counts, build time reported apart, target under 60 s
A median over target lists the slowest classes as T9's and T10's input and goes to the maintainer; no new tier
Numbers and the commit are in the delta
steps.scenario_name: The whole fast backend tier answers in under a minute and the timing column agrees with it
steps.implementation_notes: T9's budgets and every id diff key on that column, so a stripped argument there would look like a lost test. No other run beside a timed run. The wrapper script stays out of the repo. Commit: test(test-infra), then docs(test-infra).

steps.name: Docs, the last list and the closing record
steps.description: CLAUDE.md names the fast loop, mutation-testing.md warns off the old term, L7, and the closing list.
criteria: CLAUDE.md prints the safe filter or the script, never the bare one: git grep -nE 'TestCategory!=Integration([^&]|$)' -- CLAUDE.md Lighthouse.Backend/Test-Coverage.ps1 Lighthouse.Backend/Test-Fast.ps1 Scripts/test-selection docs/ci-learnings.md .claude/commands prints only the warning line of mutation-testing.md; CLAUDE.md names Test-Fast.ps1, says neither command is a gate, and says Windows is unverified
.claude/commands/mutation-testing.md has one line not to copy TestCategory!=Integration from old configs
Every classify_* answers false for the push's diff; no ci*.yml and no csproj is in it
L7, one list run of the always-on clause, against L6: Passed ids match, exempted lines aside
The closing record holds every commit against guarantee 1's allow-list, and the count of force-full runs caused by this Story's files, which is one

The DISCUSS Checklist is ticked by evidence, mutation N/A stated per slice, the watch on the first force-full run after slice E and the owed lines of T9's and T5's briefs handed over; no release notes

CLAUDE.md's DELIVER rules say, as the maintainer decided on 2026-11-07: red, green and refactor inside a step use the fast loop (pnpm test:fast --changed, pnpm test --changed for a component edit, Test-Fast.ps1 -NoBuild) plus the named test of the step, whatever its tier; the full gates run once at the end of a slice and before every push; a clean fast loop never replaces them
steps.scenario_name: A developer finds the fast loop in the docs and CI still runs every test
steps.implementation_notes: Commit: docs(test-infra). After this step the orchestrator makes push 7, which carries Scripts/test-timings/, a backend path, so it makes a plain run with no ci*.yml edit. Its CSV is cross-checked against push 6's, and its Unit rows must equal the fast list plus the 3 offline ids, both directions; that result closes guarantee 14 and goes in the delta. ADO #6512 moves by the usual story rule; the Epic is the maintainer's.
